title: Most mining sites cannot be classified as armed-held or not
detail: No public map of M23-held territory exists as data. We place 59 of 3,469 sites inside armed-group-held areas, and 48 as contested, using dated UN, NGO and media claims about specific places: by site name where sources list them, and by a small radius (our inference) around named towns. Every other site is unknown at this date, not free of armed groups. Critical Threats offers shapefiles by email request, which would extend this. Evidence stops at April 2026 for the UN and 28 October 2026 for Critical Threats.

title: The IPIS mining-site data does not record M23
detail: The map's 3,469 IPIS sites show armed presence at each researcher visit from 2009 to March 2026, but M23/AFC never appears. There are no IPIS sites in Rutshuru or Nyiragongo, and recent visits in Masisi (including Rubaya) are third-party visits that did not record armed actors. Current M23 control comes only from the key sites researched from UN, NGO and US government sources.

title: IPIS data comes from its public webmap feed, not the official download
detail: IPIS's official download sits behind a registration form and its old geoserver is offline. We used the same open data IPIS's public webmap serves to every visitor (ODC-BY licence). It has fewer fields than the full dataset, and about 13% of visit dates are year-only.

title: The January 2026 Rubaya death toll is contested
detail: Counts range from 'over 200' (M23-appointed officials) to about 400 (civil society) and over 430 bodies (a rescuer). The widely quoted '227' comes from an anonymous source whose page we could not read.

title: The UAE's share of Rwandan gold is unconfirmed
detail: Rwanda says the UAE took 63.9% of its formal goods exports in 2024 and that gold is a main export there, but we have no gold-specific figure. Check UN Comtrade HS 7108.

title: Reuters reporting on Boss Mining Solution not yet read
detail: Figures reported by Reuters (Jul 2025) are known only from search snippets and are not shown.

title: Two of ITSCI's six suspensions are not yet identified
detail: Four suspensions are verified by name and date. A reported Rani Mining suspension (Jul 2026) and one more could not be confirmed from ITSCI's own pages.

title: Sanctions have not reached the named coltan exporters
detail: US and EU sanctions hit the gold refinery, the army, the defence ministry and a bank, plus DRC-side and Hong Kong actors. None of the Rwandan coltan exporters Global Witness names has been designated.

title: Two 2026 OFAC actions not yet added
detail: Treasury's June 2026 release refers to actions on 30 Apr 2026 (Joseph Kabila) and 2 Jun 2026 (FDLR and M23 commanders). Their primary releases have not been read yet.

title: Outcome of the EU–Rwanda minerals MoU review unknown
detail: No primary Commission document on how the review ended was found.

title: Trade records cover only part of Rwanda's exports
detail: Sayari has no Rwandan customs data; most rows are Tanzanian transit records. There are no rows for 2021–22 and almost none for Jan–Aug 2024, so the trade records can't test what happened when M23 took Rubaya. Gold leaves by air and is not covered.

title: Smelter audit dates are missing, and six statuses are frozen
detail: All eight smelters were conformant in RMI data of 22 May 2026, read from a company's filing. On 17 Aug 2026 RMI paused new China assessments and extended existing ones, so the six Chinese statuses are not current audit results. Last-assessment dates are in an RMI table whose terms we have not accepted.

title: Brand links show what filings list, not what was received
detail: 41 companies are shown. No filing says a company received Rubaya material. 18 large filers checked, including Apple, Tesla, Ford, GM, Boeing and Dell, name none of the eight in the filing searched, which means no list there, not no exposure. Apple filed no Conflict Minerals Report for 2025.

title: Ownership of unsanctioned exporters rests mostly on Global Witness's documents
detail: Mixing Sayari trade records with UN and NGO reports and open registries found owners and directors for most exporters, but no Rwandan registry record could be read directly. Customs and registry records add structure, not ore origin: every armed-group link still rests on UN or NGO evidence. OpenCorporates, OCCRP Aleph and RAK ICC could not be used without login, and ACLED's open files carry no company data.

title: No source states how much of Rwanda's excess is armed-group material
detail: Our low, central and high shares are arithmetic on UN volumes with pass-through rates we chose. They could be overturned by Rwandan mine-level records, ore fingerprinting, a documented stock drawdown or non-Kivu source, or Rubaya output shown leaving by another route. Congo's statistics also conflict: 2024 coltan exports are 1,245 t in ministry tables and 2,849 t in another official series.
